sanskrit: lokavedaviruddhaṃ tvaṃ nādharmaṃ dhārmikaḥ śuciḥ kartum arhasi kaunteya kasmāt te buddhir īdṛśī
english: You, O son of Kuntī, who are righteous and pure, ought not to commit an act contrary to worldly usage and the Vedas. Why do you have such a mind?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sūkṣmo dharmo mahārāja nāsya vidmo vayaṃ gatim pūrveṣām ānupūrvyeṇa yātaṃ vartmānuyāmahe
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Dharma is subtle, O great king; we do not know its course. We follow the path trodden in succession by the ancients.

sanskrit: na me vāg anṛtaṃ prāha nādharme dhīyate matiḥ evaṃ caiva vadaty ambā mama caiva manogatam
english: My speech does not speak untruth, nor does my mind dwell on adharma. Mother speaks thus, and it accords with my own heart's resolve.

sanskrit: eṣa dharmo dhruvo rājaṃś carainam avicārayan mā ca te 'tra viśaṅkā bhūt kathaṃ cid api pārthiva
english: This is a fixed dharma, O king — follow it without hesitation. Let there be no doubt in your mind about this in any way, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: drupada uvāca tvaṃ ca kuntī ca kaunteya dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca me sutaḥ kathayantv itikartavyaṃ śvaḥ kāle karavāmahe
english: Drupada said: You, O son of Kuntī, and Kuntī, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna my son — let all discuss what is to be done. We shall act at the proper time tomorrow.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te sametya tataḥ sarve kathayanti sma bhārata atha dvaipāyano rājann abhyāgacchad yadṛcchayā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then all of them came together and were conversing, O Bhārata, when Dvaipāyana arrived there by chance, O king.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas te pāṇḍavāḥ sarve pāñcālyaś ca mahāyaśāḥ pratyutthāya mahātmānaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dṛṣṭvābhyapūjayan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then all the Pāṇḍavas and the greatly renowned son of Pāñcāla, rising to receive him, worshipped that great-souled Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana upon seeing him.

sanskrit: pratinandya sa tān sarvān pṛṣṭvā kuśalam antataḥ āsane kāñcane śubhre niṣasāda mahāmanāḥ
english: Having welcomed them all and enquired after their welfare in full, that great-minded one took his seat on a bright golden throne.

sanskrit: anujñātās tu te sarve kṛṣṇenāmitatejasā āsaneṣu mahārheṣu niṣedur dvipadāṃ varāḥ
english: Then, permitted by Kṛṣṇa of immeasurable splendour, all those foremost among men seated themselves on their respective splendid seats.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtān madhurāṃ vāṇīm uccārya pārṣataḥ papraccha taṃ mahātmānaṃ draupadyarthe viśāṃ patiḥ
english: Then, after a moment, the lord of the Pāñcālas — the son of Pṛṣata — addressed that great soul in sweet words and asked him about the matter of Draupadī.

sanskrit: katham ekā bahūnāṃ syān na ca syād dharmasaṃkaraḥ etan no bhagavān sarvaṃ prabravītu yathātatham
english: How can one woman be the wife of many, and how would there be no confusion of dharma? Let the revered one explain all this to us as it truly is.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca asmin dharme vipralambhe lokavedavirodhake yasya yasya mataṃ yad yac chrotum icchāmi tasya tat
english: Vyāsa said: In this matter of dharma that is disputed and opposed to worldly usage and the Vedas, I wish to hear whatever opinion each one holds.

sanskrit: drupada uvāca adharmo 'yaṃ mama mato viruddho lokavedayoḥ na hy ekā vidyate patnī bahūnāṃ dvijasattama
english: Drupada said: In my view this is adharma, contrary to both worldly usage and the Vedas; for one wife for many men is not known to exist, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: na cāpy ācaritaḥ pūrvair ayaṃ dharmo mahātmabhiḥ na ca dharmo 'py anekasthaś caritavyaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Nor has this dharma been practised by the great-souled ones of the past. And an eternal dharma shared among many is not to be followed.

sanskrit: ato nāhaṃ karomy evaṃ vyavasāyaṃ kriyāṃ prati dharmasaṃdehasaṃdigdhaṃ pratibhāti hi mām idam
english: Therefore I shall not carry out such a resolution in action; for this seems to me shrouded in doubt and uncertainty regarding dharma.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumna uvāca yavīyasaḥ kathaṃ bhāryāṃ jyeṣṭho bhrātā dvijarṣabha brahman samabhivarteta sadvṛttaḥ saṃs tapodhana
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna said: How, O bull among the twice-born, O brahmin, could an elder brother, being of good conduct and a storehouse of austerity, approach the wife of a younger brother?

sanskrit: na tu dharmasya sūkṣmatvād gatiṃ vidmaḥ kathaṃ cana adharmo dharma iti vā vyavasāyo na śakyate
english: Yet because of the subtlety of dharma we cannot in any way know its course. Nor can a determination be made as to what is adharma and what is dharma.

sanskrit: kartum asmadvidhair brahmaṃs tato na vyavasāmy aham pañcānāṃ mahiṣī kṛṣṇā bhavatv iti kathaṃ cana
english: This cannot be resolved by persons like us, O brahmin. Therefore I am in no way able to determine that Kṛṣṇā should be the chief queen of five men.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca na me vāg anṛtaṃ prāha nādharme dhīyate matiḥ vartate hi mano me 'tra naiṣo 'dharmaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: My speech does not speak untruth; my mind does not dwell on adharma. My heart inclines in this direction — this is in no way adharma.

sanskrit: śrūyate hi purāṇe 'pi jaṭilā nāma gautamī ṛṣīn adhyāsitavatī sapta dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: For even in ancient legend it is heard that Jaṭilā, the daughter of Gautama, dwelt with seven seers who were upholders of dharma, O best among the righteous.

sanskrit: guroś ca vacanaṃ prāhur dharmaṃ dharmajñasattama gurūṇāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ janitrī paramo guruḥ
english: They say that the word of one's teacher is dharma, O best among those who know dharma; and among all teachers the mother is the supreme teacher.

sanskrit: sā cāpy uktavatī vācaṃ bhaikṣavad bhujyatām iti tasmād etad ahaṃ manye dharmaṃ dvijavarottama
english: And she too spoke the words 'Let it be enjoyed like alms.' Therefore I consider this to be dharma, O foremost among the twice-born.

sanskrit: kunty uvāca evam etad yathāhāyaṃ dharmacārī yudhiṣṭhiraḥ anṛtān me bhayaṃ tīvraṃ mucyeyam anṛtāt katham
english: Kuntī said: It is exactly as Yudhiṣṭhira, that follower of dharma, has said. My fear of untruth is intense — how could I be freed from untruth?

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca anṛtān mokṣyase bhadre dharmaś caiṣa sanātanaḥ na tu vakṣyāmi sarveṣāṃ pāñcāla śṛṇu me svayam
english: Vyāsa said: You will be freed from untruth, O blessed one, and this is indeed the eternal dharma. But I shall not speak of it before all; O Pāñcāla, hear from me yourself.

sanskrit: yathāyaṃ vihito dharmo yataś cāyaṃ sanātanaḥ yathā ca prāha kaunteyas tathā dharmo na saṃśayaḥ
english: As this dharma has been ordained, and as it is eternal, and as the son of Kuntī has declared it — so it is dharma, without any doubt.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tata utthāya bhagavān vyāso dvaipāyanaḥ prabhuḥ kare gṛhītvā rājānaṃ rājaveśma samāviśat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the revered lord Vyāsa Dvaipāyana rose, and taking the king by the hand, entered the royal palace.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś cāpi kuntī ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ vicetasas te tatraiva pratīkṣante sma tāv ubhau
english: And the Pāṇḍavas, Kuntī, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata remained there with bewildered minds, awaiting those two.

sanskrit: tato dvaipāyanas tasmai narendrāya mahātmane ācakhyau tad yathā dharmo bahūnām ekapatnitā
english: Then Dvaipāyana related to that great-souled lord of men how one wife for many is indeed dharma.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca purā vai naimiṣāraṇye devāḥ satram upāsate tatra vaivasvato rājañ śāmitram akarot tadā
english: Vyāsa said: Long ago the gods performed a sacrifice in the Naimiṣa forest, O king. There Vaivasvata Yama then acted as the slaughterer.

sanskrit: tato yamo dīkṣitas tatra rājan; nāmārayat kiṃ cad api prajābhyaḥ tataḥ prajās tā bahulā babhūvuḥ; kālātipātān maraṇāt prahīṇāḥ
english: Then Yama, consecrated in that sacrifice, O king, did not cause the death of any living being. Thereupon the creatures multiplied greatly, freed from death through the passage of time.

sanskrit: tatas tu śakro varuṇaḥ kuberaḥ; sādhyā rudrā vasavaś cāśvinau ca praṇetāraṃ bhuvanasya prajāpatiṃ; samājagmus tatra devās tathānye
english: Then Indra, Varuṇa, Kubera, the Sādhyas, the Rudras, the Vasus, and the Aśvins, together with other gods, came to Prajāpati, the guide of the worlds.

sanskrit: tato 'bruvaṃl lokaguruṃ sametā; bhayaṃ nas tīvraṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ vivṛddhyā tasmād bhayād udvijantaḥ sukhepsavaḥ; prayāma sarve śaraṇaṃ bhavantam
english: Then, assembled together, they addressed the teacher of the worlds: 'We have intense fear from the multiplication of humans. Trembling from that fear, all of us who seek happiness come to you as our refuge.'

sanskrit: brahmovāca kiṃ vo bhayaṃ mānuṣebhyo yūyaṃ sarve yadāmarāḥ mā vo martyasakāśād vai bhayaṃ bhavatu karhi cit
english: Brahmā said: What fear have you of mortals, you who are all immortals? Let there never be any fear for you from the presence of mortal beings.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ martyā hy amartyāḥ saṃvṛttā na viśeṣo 'sti kaś cana aviśeṣād udvijanto viśeṣārtham ihāgatāḥ
english: The gods said: The mortals have become as immortals — there is no distinction whatsoever. Troubled by this lack of distinction, we have come here seeking distinction.

sanskrit: brahmovāca vaivasvato vyāpṛtaḥ satrahetos; tena tv ime na mriyante manuṣyāḥ tasminn ekāgre kṛtasarvakārye; tata eṣāṃ bhavitaivāntakālaḥ
english: Brahmā said: Vaivasvata is occupied with the sacrifice; that is why these humans do not die. When his single-pointed attention is finished with that task, the time of their end will come.

sanskrit: vaivasvatasyāpi tanur vibhūtā; vīryeṇa yuṣmākam uta prayuktā saiṣām anto bhavitā hy antakāle; tanur hi vīryaṃ bhavitā nareṣu
english: And the body of Vaivasvata, made mighty and set in motion by your collective power — that shall be their end at the time of their ending; for that body shall become the force of death among men.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca tatas tu te pūrvajadevavākyaṃ; śrutvā devā yatra devā yajante samāsīnās te sametā mahābalā; bhāgīrathyāṃ dadṛśuḥ puṇḍarīkam
english: Vyāsa said: Then the gods, having heard the words of the elder god, went to where the gods were performing the sacrifice. Seated together, those mighty ones saw a lotus on the Bhāgīrathī.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca tad vismitās te babhūvus; teṣām indras tatra śūro jagāma so 'paśyad yoṣām atha pāvakaprabhāṃ; yatra gaṅgā satataṃ saṃprasūtā
english: Seeing it, they were filled with wonder. Indra the heroic one went there among them, and he saw a woman of blazing splendour where the Gaṅgā ever flows forth.

sanskrit: sā tatra yoṣā rudatī jalārthinī; gaṅgāṃ devīṃ vyavagāhyāvatiṣṭhat tasyāśrubinduḥ patito jale vai; tat padmam āsīd atha tatra kāñcanam
english: That woman, weeping and longing for water, plunged into the goddess Gaṅgā and stood there. A teardrop of hers fell into the water, and from it arose that golden lotus.

sanskrit: tad adbhutaṃ prekṣya vajrī tadānīm; apṛcchat tāṃ yoṣitam antikād vai kā tvaṃ kathaṃ rodiṣi kasya hetor; vākyaṃ tathyaṃ kāmayeha bravīhi
english: Seeing that wonder, the wielder of the thunderbolt then approached near and asked that woman: 'Who are you? Why do you weep and for what reason? I desire you to speak the truth here.'

sanskrit: stry uvāca tvaṃ vetsyase mām iha yāsmi śakra; yadarthaṃ cāhaṃ rodimi mandabhāgyā āgaccha rājan purato 'haṃ gamiṣye; draṣṭāsi tad rodimi yatkṛte 'ham
english: The woman said: You will come to know who I am here, O Śakra, and the reason why I, the ill-fortuned one, weep. Come, O king, I will go before you — you shall see that for the sake of which I weep.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca tāṃ gacchantīm anvagacchat tadānīṃ; so 'paśyad ārāt taruṇaṃ darśanīyam siṃhāsanasthaṃ yuvatīsahāyaṃ; krīḍantam akṣair girirājamūrdhni
english: Vyāsa said: He followed her as she went, and then from a distance he saw a handsome young man seated on a lion-throne with a young woman as his companion, playing at dice on the summit of the king of mountains.

sanskrit: tam abravīd devarājo mamedaṃ; tvaṃ viddhi viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ vaśe sthitam īśo 'ham asmīti samanyur abravīd; dṛṣṭvā tam akṣaiḥ subhṛśaṃ pramattam
english: The king of gods addressed him angrily: 'Know that this entire world is under my power — I am the lord.' So he spoke with indignation, seeing him wholly absorbed in dice.

sanskrit: kruddhaṃ tu śakraṃ prasamīkṣya devo; jahāsa śakraṃ ca śanair udaikṣata saṃstambhito 'bhūd atha devarājas; tenekṣitaḥ sthāṇur ivāvatasthe
english: But the god, looking steadily at the wrathful Śakra, laughed, and gazed at Śakra calmly. Then the king of gods became paralysed, looked upon by him, and stood stiff as a post.

sanskrit: yadā tu paryāptam ihāsya krīḍayā; tadā devīṃ rudatīṃ tām uvāca ānīyatām eṣa yato 'ham ārān; mainaṃ darpaḥ punar apy āviśeta
english: When at last his play here was completed, he addressed that weeping goddess: 'Let this one be brought from where I came — so that arrogance may not enter him again.'

sanskrit: tataḥ śakraḥ spṛṣṭamātras tayā tu; srastair aṅgaiḥ patito 'bhūd dharaṇyām tam abravīd bhagavān ugratejā; maivaṃ punaḥ śakra kṛthāḥ kathaṃ cit
english: Then Śakra, merely touched by her, fell to the ground with limbs gone limp. The revered one of fierce splendour addressed him: 'Do not act thus again, O Śakra, in any way.'

sanskrit: vivartayainaṃ ca mahādrirājaṃ; balaṃ ca vīryaṃ ca tavāprameyam vivṛtya caivāviśa madhyam asya; yatrāsate tvadvidhāḥ sūryabhāsaḥ
english: Roll open this great mountain king, and behold your own immeasurable strength and might. Having opened it, enter its interior, where others like you, blazing like the sun, are seated.

sanskrit: sa tad vivṛtya śikharaṃ mahāgires; tulyadyutīṃś caturo 'nyān dadarśa sa tān abhiprekṣya babhūva duḥkhitaḥ; kaccin nāhaṃ bhavitā vai yatheme
english: He opened that peak of the great mountain and saw four others equal in splendour. Gazing upon them he became grieved: 'Shall I too become like these?'

sanskrit: tato devo giriśo vajrapāṇiṃ; vivṛtya netre kupito 'bhyuvāca darīm etāṃ praviśa tvaṃ śatakrato; yan māṃ bālyād avamaṃsthāḥ purastāt
english: Then the god Giriśa, opening his eyes, addressed the wielder of the thunderbolt in anger: 'Enter this cave, O Śatakratu — because in your childishness you disrespected me before.'

sanskrit: uktas tv evaṃ vibhunā devarājaḥ; pravepamāno bhṛśam evābhiṣaṅgāt srastair aṅgaiḥ anileneva nunnam; aśvatthapatraṃ girirājamūrdhni
english: Thus addressed by the mighty one, the king of gods trembled violently with anguish, his limbs gone limp, like an aśvattha leaf driven by the wind on the summit of the mountain king.

sanskrit: sa prāñjalir vinatenānanena; pravepamānaḥ sahasaivam uktaḥ uvāca cedaṃ bahurūpam ugraṃ; draṣṭā śeṣasya bhagavaṃs tvaṃ bhavādya
english: He, with folded hands and bowed face, trembling, suddenly so addressed, spoke to the many-formed and terrible one: 'You, O revered one, will today be the witness of the remainder.'

sanskrit: tam abravīd ugradhanvā prahasya; naivaṃśīlāḥ śeṣam ihāpnuvanti ete 'py evaṃ bhavitāraḥ purastāt; tasmād etāṃ darim āviśya śedhvam
english: The wielder of the fierce bow laughed and said to him: 'Those of such character do not attain a remainder here. These too shall be thus hereafter. Therefore enter this cave and remain.'

sanskrit: śeṣo 'py evaṃ bhavitā vo na saṃśayo; yoniṃ sarve mānuṣīm āviśadhvam tatra yūyaṃ karma kṛtvāviṣahyaṃ; bahūn anyān nidhanaṃ prāpayitvā
english: The remainder of your time will also be thus — there is no doubt. All of you shall enter a human womb. There, having performed irresistible deeds and having brought many others to destruction—

sanskrit: āgantāraḥ punar evendralokaṃ; svakarmaṇā pūrvajitaṃ mahārham sarvaṃ mayā bhāṣitam etad evaṃ; kartavyam anyad vividhārthavac ca
english: —you shall return again to Indra's realm, that great and worthy abode won previously by your own deeds. All this has been spoken by me as it is. Other things of various purposes are also to be done.

sanskrit: pūrvendrā ūcuḥ gamiṣyāmo mānuṣaṃ devalokād; durādharo vihito yatra mokṣaḥ devās tv asmān ādadhīrañ jananyāṃ; dharmo vāyur maghavān aśvinau ca
english: The former Indras said: We shall go from the world of gods to the human world where the ordained liberation is hard to attain. But let the gods place us in a mother's womb — Dharma, Vāyu, Maghavan, and the Aśvins.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca etac chrutvā vajrapāṇir vacas tu; devaśreṣṭhaṃ punar evedam āha vīryeṇāhaṃ puruṣaṃ kāryahetor; dadyām eṣāṃ pañcamaṃ matprasūtam
english: Vyāsa said: Hearing these words, the wielder of the thunderbolt addressed the best of gods again: 'I will give, through my power and for the purpose of this task, a fifth man to them, born from myself.'

sanskrit: teṣāṃ kāmaṃ bhagavān ugradhanvā; prādād iṣṭaṃ sannisargād yathoktam tāṃ cāpy eṣāṃ yoṣitaṃ lokakāntāṃ; śriyaṃ bhāryāṃ vyadadhān mānuṣeṣu
english: The revered wielder of the fierce bow granted their desire, giving what was sought through divine release as spoken. And that woman beloved of the world, Śrī herself, he ordained as their wife among men.

sanskrit: tair eva sārdhaṃ tu tataḥ sa devo; jagāma nārāyaṇam aprameyam sa cāpi tad vyadadhāt sarvam eva; tataḥ sarve saṃbabhūvur dharaṇyām
english: Then that god went together with those very ones to the immeasurable Nārāyaṇa. He too ordained all of it. Thereupon all of them were born upon the earth.

sanskrit: sa cāpi keśau harir udbabarha; śuklam ekam aparaṃ cāpi kṛṣṇam tau cāpi keśau viśatāṃ yadūnāṃ; kule striyau rohiṇīṃ devakīṃ ca tayor eko baladevo babhūva; kṛṣṇo dvitīyaḥ keśavaḥ saṃbabhūva
english: And Hari plucked two hairs from himself — one white and one black. Those two hairs entered two women of the Yadu clan, Rohiṇī and Devakī. From them, one became Baladeva, and the second became Kṛṣṇa Keśava.

sanskrit: ye te pūrvaṃ śakrarūpā niruddhās; tasyāṃ daryāṃ parvatasyottarasya ihaiva te pāṇḍavā vīryavantaḥ; śakrasyāṃśaḥ pāṇḍavaḥ savyasācī
english: Those who previously, bearing Indra's form, were confined in that cave of the northern mountain — they are here the mighty Pāṇḍavas. The Pāṇḍava Savyasācī is a portion of Indra.

sanskrit: evam ete pāṇḍavāḥ saṃbabhūvur; ye te rājan pūrvam indrā babhūvuḥ lakṣmīś caiṣāṃ pūrvam evopadiṣṭā; bhāryā yaiṣā draupadī divyarūpā
english: Thus these Pāṇḍavas were born, O king — those who were formerly Indras. And Lakṣmī herself was earlier ordained for them; this Draupadī of divine form is their wife.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi strī karmaṇo 'nte mahītalāt; samuttiṣṭhed anyato daivayogāt yasyā rūpaṃ somasūryaprakāśaṃ; gandhaś cāgryaḥ krośamātrāt pravāti
english: For how else could a woman arise from the earth at the end of a ritual act other than through divine dispensation — she whose beauty shines like the moon and sun, and whose supreme fragrance wafts a league away?

sanskrit: idaṃ cānyat prītipūrvaṃ narendra; dadāmi te varam atyadbhutaṃ ca divyaṃ cakṣuḥ paśya kuntīsutāṃs tvaṃ; puṇyair divyaiḥ pūrvadehair upetān
english: And this other boon I give you gladly, O lord of men — a most wonderful one: divine sight. See the sons of Kuntī endowed with their blessed and divine former bodies.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato vyāsaḥ paramodārakarmā; śucir vipras tapasā tasya rājñaḥ cakṣur divyaṃ pradadau tān sa sarvān; rājāpaśyat pūrvadehair yathāvat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Vyāsa, that brahmin of supremely noble deeds, pure through his austerity, bestowed divine sight on the king. The king saw all of them as they truly were in their former bodies.

sanskrit: tato divyān hemakirīṭamālinaḥ; śakraprakhyān pāvakādityavarṇān baddhāpīḍāṃś cārurūpāṃś ca yūno; vyūḍhoraskāṃs tālamātrān dadarśa
english: Then he saw them divine, wearing golden crowns and garlands, resembling Indra, of the colour of fire and sun, wearing bound diadems, handsome and youthful, broad-chested, of the height of a palm tree.

sanskrit: divyair vastrair arajobhiḥ suvarṇair; mālyaiś cāgryaiḥ śobhamānān atīva sākṣāt tryakṣān vasavo vātha divyān; ādityān vā sarvaguṇopapannān tān pūrvendrān evam īkṣyābhirūpān; prīto rājā drupado vismitaś ca
english: Adorned most brilliantly with divine spotless golden garments and finest garlands, they were like the Three-eyed one himself, or the divine Vasus, or the Ādityas possessed of every virtue. Seeing those former Indras so handsome, king Drupada was delighted and full of wonder.

sanskrit: divyāṃ māyāṃ tām avāpyāprameyāṃ; tāṃ caivāgryāṃ śriyam iva rūpiṇīṃ ca yogyāṃ teṣāṃ rūpatejoyaśobhiḥ; patnīm ṛddhāṃ dṛṣṭavān pārthivendraḥ
english: And having attained that immeasurable divine māyā, the lord of earth saw her too — that foremost one, like Śrī incarnate, worthy of them by her beauty, splendour, and fame — their glorious wife.

sanskrit: sa tad dṛṣṭvā mahad āścaryarūpaṃ; jagrāha pādau satyavatyāḥ sutasya naitac citraṃ paramarṣe tvayīti; prasannacetāḥ sa uvāca cainam
english: Having seen that great and wondrous form, he clasped the feet of the son of Satyavatī. With serene mind he addressed him: 'This is no marvel for you, O supreme seer.'

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca āsīt tapovane kā cid ṛṣeḥ kanyā mahātmanaḥ nādhyagacchat patiṃ sā tu kanyā rūpavatī satī
english: Vyāsa said: In a hermitage forest there was once a daughter of a great-souled seer. That maiden, though beautiful and virtuous, could not find a husband.

sanskrit: toṣayām āsa tapasā sā kilogreṇa śaṃkaram tām uvāceśvaraḥ prīto vṛṇu kāmam iti svayam
english: She propitiated Śaṃkara with fierce austerity. The Lord, well pleased, personally told her: 'Choose your boon.'

sanskrit: saivam uktābravīt kanyā devaṃ varadam īśvaram patiṃ sarvaguṇopetam icchāmīti punaḥ punaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the maiden said to the god, the granter of boons, the Lord: 'I desire a husband endowed with every virtue' — saying this again and again.

sanskrit: dadau tasyai sa deveśas taṃ varaṃ prītimāṃs tadā pañca te patayaḥ śreṣṭhā bhaviṣyantīti śaṃkaraḥ
english: The lord of gods, Śaṃkara, joyfully granted her that boon then: 'Five noble husbands shall be yours.'

sanskrit: sā prasādayatī devam idaṃ bhūyo 'bhyabhāṣata ekaṃ patiṃ guṇopetaṃ tvatto 'rhāmīti vai tadā tāṃ devadevaḥ prītātmā punaḥ prāha śubhaṃ vacaḥ
english: She, still entreating the god, spoke again: 'I deserve one husband endowed with virtue from you.' Then the god of gods, with joyful heart, spoke again an auspicious word to her.

sanskrit: pañcakṛtvas tvayā uktaḥ patiṃ dehīty ahaṃ punaḥ tat tathā bhavitā bhadre tava tad bhadram astu te deham anyaṃ gatāyās te yathoktaṃ tad bhaviṣyati
english: 'Five times you have said to me: give me a husband — again. So shall it be, O fortunate one; may good come to you. When you have gone to another body, what was spoken shall come to pass for you.'

sanskrit: drupadaiṣā hi sā jajñe sutā te devarūpiṇī pañcānāṃ vihitā patnī kṛṣṇā pārṣaty aninditā
english: She is this very one who was born as Drupada's daughter, of divine form. The blameless Kṛṣṇā, daughter of Pṛṣata, has been ordained as wife to five.

sanskrit: svargaśrīḥ pāṇḍavārthāya samutpannā mahāmakhe seha taptvā tapo ghoraṃ duhitṛtvaṃ tavāgatā
english: The glory of heaven, born in a great sacrifice for the sake of the Pāṇḍavas — having here performed fierce austerity, she has come to be your daughter.

sanskrit: saiṣā devī rucirā devajuṣṭā; pañcānām ekā svakṛtena karmaṇā sṛṣṭā svayaṃ devapatnī svayambhuvā; śrutvā rājan drupadeṣṭaṃ kuruṣva
english: This resplendent goddess, beloved of the gods, is one wife for five by her own past deed — she herself created as wife of the gods by the Self-born. Having heard, O king, do what Drupada desires.

sanskrit: drupada uvāca aśrutvaivaṃ vacanaṃ te maharṣe; mayā pūrvaṃ yatitaṃ kāryam etat na vai śakyaṃ vihitasyāpayātuṃ; tad evedam upapannaṃ vidhānam
english: Drupada said: Without having heard such words from you, O great seer, I had earlier striven in this matter. Indeed what has been ordained cannot be averted — the very same ordinance has come to pass.

sanskrit: diṣṭasya granthir anivartanīyaḥ; svakarmaṇā vihitaṃ neha kiṃ cit kṛtaṃ nimittaṃ hi varaikahetos; tad evedam upapannaṃ bahūnām
english: The knot of destiny is not to be undone; nothing here is ordained by one's own action alone. Indeed what was brought about as the cause for the one boon — that very thing has now come to pass for many.

sanskrit: yathaiva kṛṣṇoktavatī purastān; naikān patīn me bhagavān dadātu sa cāpy evaṃ varam ity abravīt tāṃ; devo hi veda paramaṃ yad atra
english: Just as Kṛṣṇā previously said 'Let the revered one grant me not many husbands,' and he too replied to her with the boon thus — the god indeed knows what is supreme in this matter.
